title: I used code to test the interaction model.
intro: For this project, I worked across PM, product design, design engineering and Vibe Coding. A runnable prototype let me examine the relationships that static screens could not answer: what continues when a shot changes, what selection refers to, and which timeline should appear.
I carried the work from defining the product and interaction rules through implementation, iteration and delivery, collaborating with two engineers whose main focus was Agent-side capabilities.

items.label: PRODUCT & DESIGN
items.title: Define the behavior.
items.text: Frame the creator tasks, choose the white-block scope, map scene / camera / shot relationships, and specify how a local edit should behave.

items.label: DESIGN ENGINEERING
items.title: Make the decisions tangible.
items.text: Use executable prototypes and Vibe Coding to build and iterate the experience, revealing edge cases in selection, movement, framing and sequencing.

items.label: TEAM DELIVERY
items.title: Connect the whole workflow.
items.text: Align the editing experience with Agent targeting and revision handling, prepare test tasks and onboarding, and follow issues through to delivery.

body: This changed the nature of review. Instead of discussing whether a static layout looked simpler, I could put a concrete task through the editor and examine what the next interaction actually did.
